title: Centralist Mexico
capsule: Centralist Mexico (la República Centralista) was the unitary regime that governed the Mexican state from 1835–1836 until 1846, after conservatives repealed the federalist 1824 Constitution and promulgated the Siete Leyes ("Seven Laws") in December 1836, which abolished the sovereign states and reorganized them into departments with governors appointed from Mexico City. The era was dominated by Antonio López de Santa Anna and Anastasio Bustamante and saw the secession of Texas in 1836—after Santa Anna's capture at San Jacinto—and the revolt of Yucatán, while resisting the French blockade of Veracruz in the Pastry War (1838–1839). A second centralist charter, the Bases Orgánicas, followed in 1843, but mounting losses in the U.S.–Mexican War prompted the restoration of the 1824 federal constitution in August 1846, ending the centralist experiment.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Mexico's modern borders are defined by treaties — the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo (1848) and Gadsden Purchase (1853) with the United States, and the Chamizal Convention (1963) — and are precisely documented; internal state boundaries are well-mapped.
